items.title: Your Next Great Read Might Be Certified ‘Organic’
items.excerpt: Amid a sea of AI writing slop, a new stamp for “organic literature” will help readers pick out books authored by real humans.

items.title: ‘We have fine dining, and we have McDonalds’: Publishers hotly debate AI narration at FBF
items.excerpt: Publishers from Blinkist, Storytel and Hörbuch Hamburg Verlag debated the value of AI narration on a Frankfurt Book Fair panel on 7 October.

items.title: Pangram CEO says ‘no bias’ in its AI-detection tool, as adoption rises
items.excerpt: Pangram's co-founder defended its AI detection tool against claims it penalises authors of colour, citing a huge upswing in adoption by publishers.

items.title: Sales of Thélyson Orélien's novel skyrocket despite AI and plagiarism accusations
items.excerpt: A fortnight after an X account accused Orélien of writing most of his award-winning novel with generative AI, sales have surged rather than dipped.

items.title: S&S Staff Balk at AI Performance-Tracking Software Talks
items.excerpt: Simon & Schuster employees are circulating an open letter opposing use of Skan AI or similar software to monitor their work; the CEO says there is no company-wide rollout.

items.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: Five Questions with Elisabeth Jaquette
items.excerpt: The executive director of Words Without Borders on why translated literature matters and why the organization is rejecting AI translation.

items.title: TRACE Project Launches to Advance AI interoperability
items.excerpt: The scholarly publishing community launches TRACE, a project to improve generative AI systems' interoperability, verifiability and usage tracking of licensed content.

items.title: Barrierefreies Lesen und KI-gestützte Hörbuchproduktion
items.excerpt: The 2026 Digital Publishing Award, presented at Frankfurt on 7 October, honours Avneesh Singh, Nahdet Misr Group, Pozotron Studio (AI-assisted audiobook production) and ReadBee from 42 entries.

items.title: KI in Büchern: Schreiben nein, Übersetzen ja?
items.excerpt: 79 percent of respondents in a new survey support AI for book translation, but only 29 percent would read a book written entirely by AI.

items.title: Neues Label: "Von Menschen gemacht"
items.excerpt: 18 German-language children's and YA publishers launch a 'written, designed, checked by humans' label to show text, illustration and design were made without generative AI.

items.title: How to Listen to Kindle Books With CastReader
items.excerpt: A guide to CastReader, which reads Kindle Cloud Reader books aloud with cloud AI voices and offers an 'AI Explain' feature for difficult passages.

items.title: From Story Seeds To Stories, And Writing An Author’s Note, With Joanna Penn
items.excerpt: Joanna Penn on turning story ideas into fiction and why an author's note matters in an age of AI; intro covers KDP's two-titles-per-week cap and AI-related Digital Publishing Awards at Frankfurt.
